coverage.main: Read all nineteen pages of arXiv 1812.00891v3 (USENIX Security 2020): Sections 1-7 including Q1-Q5 experiments, Tables 1-9, Figures 1-16, references and Appendices A-C (implementation details, parameter Tables 11-12, additional results Tables 10, 13-14, Figures 17-19).
coverage.supplement: Appendices are embedded in the arXiv PDF and read. The USENIX version was not retrieved.
coverage.excluded_results: Tables 3-8, 10, 13-14 and Figures 4-13, 15-19 evaluate ADV2/PGD/STADV against the attacked classifier-interpreter pair itself (white-box), detection-based and adversarial-training countermeasures, or the ISIC case study. None transfers adversarial inputs to a different classifier.

result_groups.population: A random set of ADV2 inputs crafted against one interpreter (GRAD, CAM, MASK, RTS) on ResNet-50, drawn from 1,000 ImageNet validation images the classifier classifies correctly; interpretations recomputed with each other interpreter on the same classifier
result_groups.outcome: L1 distance between adversarial and benign attribution maps on the target interpreter
result_groups.evidence: The classifier is shared between source and target, so no prediction transfers across models; the transferred quantity is interpretation quality. The test set is clean-correct for the shared classifier, but no clean-correct event is defined for interpretation, and the paper does not say whether only successful ADV2 inputs were sampled.

f1.evidence: Classifier top-1 accuracies (77.15%, 77.92%) and clean localization performance of all four interpreters with ResNet (Table 2) are reported, positive baseline evidence, but interpretation quality is not a classification clean accuracy.

f2.evidence: Images are selected as correctly classified by the shared classifier; the field's target-clean-correct event does not map onto an interpretation-distance outcome.

f3.evidence: 'We randomly select a set of adversarial inputs crafted against g' without stating whether unsuccessful ones are included.

f4.evidence: Mean L1 distances over an unstated number of sampled inputs; counts are not the relevant record.

f5.evidence: PGD-based ADV2 and PGD use an L-infinity threshold epsilon = 0.031 on [0,1] pixels, which covers the transfer experiment.

f6.evidence: A repository alps-lab/adv2 (276 files) provides attack, interpreter and distance scripts; it is not linked from the reviewed text, and its coverage of the Table 9 experiment and model/masking-model checkpoints were not verified.

artifact_checks.result: Found by exact-title search; listed via the GitHub API (276 files, head 17 June 2021): expr_attacks (CAM, Grad-CAM, MASK, RTS generators), distance scripts per interpreter and ISIC scripts. Not linked in the paper text reviewed; not executed.

bounds_checks.reason: Attribution-map distance on a shared classifier is not a cross-model misclassification probability.

limitations: Non-blind evidence audit. Cross-interpreter transfer is retained as an in-scope 'other attack outcome' because the attacked system component (interpreter) differs; an independent recoder could treat it as out of scope.
